en: The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and is endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, holds the judicial power to interpret the country's laws.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of Luzon over two thousand years ago.
During the Sinulog Festival in Cebu, devotees dance in the streets to honor the Santo Niño.
Filipino and English are the two official languages of the Philippines, alongside over a hundred regional languages like Cebuano.
Dr. Fe del Mundo created a makeshift incubator using two nested bamboo baskets to help rural Filipino babies.
The Philippines is divided into seventeen administrative regions, including the Cordillera Administrative Region and the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region.
Every Filipino citizen must secure a national identification card, like the PhilSys ID, to prove their identity.
The tradition of bayanihan involves neighbors physically carrying a traditional nipa hut to help a family relocate.
